recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Future changes to resolve-as-version-specific edge cases, extension definition examples, or broader Bundle reference-resolution behavior should be handled by their own Jira decisions rather than by reopening FHIR-34344.
issue_request: FHIR-34344 asked to replace broad FHIR-14138 wording that said arbitrary version references would be re-assigned, because that wording could imply that references to already-existing historical versions should also be rewritten. The approved Published/Persuasive with Modification resolution says existing version-specific references are expected to point to already-existing versions, while references to versions created by the transaction should be version-independent references carrying resolve-as-version-specific.
initial_application: HL7/fhir commit a7810f9b2cfc9f747d876079d688ce062f3af0b2 explicitly applied FHIR-34344 to source/http.html. Current source/http.html contains the replacement paragraphs and no longer contains the superseded 'arbitrarily chosen version references', 're-assigned anyway', or 'Version-specific references should remain as version-specific references' wording.
additional_context: FHIR-34343 approved the resolve-as-version-specific extension mechanism that FHIR-34344 relies on, and the extension source now lives in the FHIR Extension Pack. FHIR-I minutes on 2022-04-11 corroborate the FHIR-34344 14-0-1 persuasive-with-modification vote. The Zulip discussion around resolving references in Bundles supports the interpretation that /_history should not be appended to urn:uuid temporary transaction references. Later FHIR-37573 and FHIR-38648 addressed duplicate paragraph and link defects in the same text; those are separate later cleanups and are already represented on the combined branch.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No core source edit was needed because current source/http.html already distinguishes existing version-specific references from transaction-created versions, links to resolve-as-version-specific for the latter case, and preserves the approved dependency guidance.
